sample_unit: patients (surgical videos; 56 biportal SNUBH, 60 uniportal SEA)

links.outcome: Segmentation DSC on internal, temporal external, and cross-dataset external test sets with patient-level splits
links.effect: Foundation-model pipeline ranked last on cross-dataset external testing (DSC 0.776) with biportal-only training, about 9 points below DeepLabV3+ (0.865); external testing exposed a performance drop.
links.quote: With biportal-only training, the fully automatic foundation-model pipeline ranked last on cross-dataset external testing (DSC 0.776; 0.737 under a strict empty-mask convention), about 9% points below DeepLabV3+ (0.865).

links.outcome: Effect of adding uniportal data to training on external segmentation accuracy
links.effect: With combined training all seven pipelines exceeded DSC 0.94; the foundation-model pipeline rose from 0.776 to 0.962, driven primarily by detector rather than segmentor learning.
links.quote: With combined training, all seven pipelines exceeded DSC 0.94; nnU-Net was highest (0.978), and the foundation-model pipeline (0.962) was not significantly different from SegFormer-B0 (0.960) or DeepLabV3+ (0.958) after Bonferroni correction, although the small external sample does not establish equivalence.

links.outcome: Deployment-mode (automatic detector-prompted) versus oracle bounding-box-prompted performance
links.effect: MedSAM2-Tiny reached DSC 0.946 with ground-truth box prompts versus 0.776 fully automatic, a 16.9-point oracle-to-deployment gap; 61% missed detections and 39% box-localization error.
links.quote: The same MedSAM2-Tiny segmentor reached DSC 0.946 with ground-truth bounding-box prompts, leaving a 16.9-point oracle-to-deployment gap driven by detector domain mismatch: 61% missed detections and 39% box-localization error.

unlisted_practices: Reporting deployment DSC alongside the ground-truth bounding-box upper bound in surgical segmentation benchmarks
Benchmarking real-time inference speed against a 30 frames-per-second threshold

screen.reason: Evaluates and benchmarks multiple computer vision architectures (including foundation models like MedSAM2) for surgical instrument segmentation across datasets under deployment-realistic offline conditions, focusing on model pipeline accuracy and detector dependency rather than testing an organizational deployment safeguard.
